judgments.reasoning_cat1: One descriptive sentence about the instructional nature of activities; no term carries a contestable boundary and no obligation is created. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the risk recitals and with c018's allocation of suitability decisions to the student. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "NOLS is not responsible for the acts or omissions of such contractors" is an operative disclaimer buried in a risk bullet, and "private contractors" is undefined against the illustrative "including, for example, transportation" — a general/specific scope question. Whether a given provider is a "contractor" or an "agent" is exactly the kind of line a court is asked to draw.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c017 defines "Released Parties" as NOLS's "officers, trustees, agents, and staff including employees, volunteers and interns" and conspicuously omits contractors, while c009 lumps "contractors" with instructors and staff whose misjudgments are assumed; the three provisions treat contractors inconsistently. That is a specific, identifiable incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An acknowledgment of having read external documents, incorporating by reference materials described loosely as "other material provided by NOLS describing or related to my program" — an open-ended catch-all whose reach is genuinely uncertain. Whether those outside materials become part of the bargain is a real construction question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against c024's integration-flavoured statement that the agreement covers "this page and the previous 3 pages" and may be modified only in writing, since this clause gestures at extrinsic catalogue and website content. The tension is modest but nameable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out — "except with respect to an injury or other loss which occurs on lands whose rules or regulations prohibit my doing so as a matter of law" — is a genuinely opaque exception whose trigger (which lands, whose rules) a court would have to construe, and "ALL risks ... inherent or otherwise" is deliberately unbounded. This is the operative assumption-of-risk clause and the natural focus of any dispute over the agreement's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with c017, which limits the release to ordinary negligence and excludes gross negligence and intentional conduct; assuming "ALL risks ... whether or not described above" arguably sweeps in conduct the release expressly preserves. That is a specific internal tension between the two central operative clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core release and indemnity: "any and all claims ... arising in whole or part from ... enrollment or participation in an activity of NOLS," the enumerated-then-open "Released Parties" list, the parenthetical definition of "indemnify," the negligence/gross-negligence line, and the lands-based carve-out all supply nameable ambiguities. Exculpatory clauses of this kind are construed strictly against the drafter, and this one is drafted wholly one-sidedly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against c016 (assumption of ALL risks with no gross-negligence carve-out), c014 (contractors excluded from responsibility yet absent from the Released Parties list) and c024 (binding on heirs and estate, though heirs never signed) — several concrete points of friction. Those cross-references make a whole-instrument argument readily available.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains a warranty of medical disclosure alongside "otherwise satisfied NOLS," "any medical condition that might affect ... participation" and a discretionary right to remove a student "for any reason it deems in the best interests of the student or the school" — each a vague standard capable of two readings. The unlimited discretion phrase is the clearest candidate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with c019 (authorisation to provide care) and c011 (limits on monitoring) without direct contradiction, though the disclaimer that admission is no representation about managing emergencies sits uneasily with c019's promise of care under written Medical Protocols. The friction is arguable but soft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Costs reasonably associated with medical services, including evacuation, shall be borne by me" turns on "reasonably associated," and the reference to care "under the guidance of the NOLS Physician Advisor by way of NOLS' written Medical Protocols" incorporates an unattached document. Those are identifiable but modest ambiguities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undertaking that care "will be provided" under the Medical Protocols is in some tension with c018's disclaimer of any representation that staff can manage a medical event and with c017's release of negligence claims. A plaintiff could plausibly argue the Protocols create a standard the release disclaims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Strategic partners in which NOLS graduates may be interested" is loose, but the permission granted is plain and one-directional. Little practical scope for competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses privacy, publicity or data sharing, so nothing contradicts it. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, plain allocations of loss; "any damage" is broad but its application is straightforward and "personal belongings stored at NOLS facilities" is reasonably bounded. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs in parallel with the indemnity in c017 without duplicating or contradicting it. No inconsistency identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any mediation or suit shall occur or be filed only in the State of Wyoming" is the classic ambiguity between courts of Wyoming and courts in Wyoming, and "any mediation" appears although no mediation obligation exists anywhere in the document. The parenthetical excluding renvoi is also awkwardly phrased.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument establishes a mediation procedure, so the reference to "any mediation" hangs unsupported; the clause otherwise coexists with the severability clause (c023) and the release. That orphan reference is a real but limited whole-instrument point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional severability sentence; "any part" and "invalid" are standard and the operation is clear on its face. Little intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the carve-outs in c016 and c017 for lands whose rules prohibit such agreements, and a party could argue those carve-outs, not severance, govern partial invalidity. That overlap is worth noting but the provisions can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It purports to bind "THEIR HEIRS, ESTATE, EXECUTORS AND ADMINISTRATORS" — persons who did not sign — and recites that the signer has read "THIS PAGE AND THE PREVIOUS 3 PAGES," a page count that could mismatch the document as executed; "MODIFIED ONLY IN WRITING" is otherwise plain. The heirs language is exactly what is fought over in a wrongful-death or survivorship claim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against c017's release of claims for "injury, disability, death," the binding-on-heirs sentence is the hook for arguing the release reaches derivative claims, while c001 contemplates only student and parent signatures; and the write-only modification term sits against c015's incorporation of outside materials. Those cross-provision links give a court something to reconcile.
